                    ### Question

Despite appropriate lifesaving measures, the newborn dies 2 hours later. Autopsy shows bilateral renal agenesis. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this newborn's respiratory distress?

opb. Injury to the diaphragmatic innervation
opc. Displacement of intestines into the pleural cavity
opd. Collapse of the supraglottic airway
ope. Surfactant inactivation and epithelial inflammation

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):

The chain of events starting from bilateral renal agenesis causing oligohydramnios, which in turn results in lung underdevelopment and subsequent respiratory distress, is well-supported by medical consensus. The evidence path linking congenital absence of kidneys syndrome to anhydramnios further reinforces the relationship between renal impairment and decreased amniotic fluid. Therefore, decreased amniotic fluid ingestion is the most likely cause of the respiratory distress in this case.
